builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
summary: The technique replaces standard gradient inversion attacks (such as GIAS) with a spatially anchored generative framework that introduces server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings during client fine-tuning to create spatial anchors for reconstruction. It requires modifying client-side ViT architectures to include these trainable positional embeddings and increases server-side computational cost for the generative inversion process. Success depends on client adoption of the modified architecture; without client-side implementation of the positional embedding changes, the spatial anchoring mechanism fails and reconstruction quality degrades to baseline levels.
rationale: Relevant for engineers deploying federated LoRA systems to understand privacy vulnerabilities, but requires architectural modifications to client models and represents an attack vector rather than a production optimization technique.

claims.statement: The technique replaces standard gradient inversion attacks (such as GIAS) with a spatially anchored generative framework that introduces server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings during client fine-tuning to create spatial anchors for reconstruction. It requires modifying client-side ViT architectures to include these trainable positional embeddings and increases server-side computational cost for the generative inversion process. Success depends on client adoption of the modified architecture; without client-side implementation of the positional embedding changes, the spatial anchoring mechanism fails and reconstruction quality degrades to baseline levels.

Improves reconstruction PSNR by 10.14 dB, SSIM by 0.45, and LPIPS by 0.098 on CIFAR-10, with PSNR gains of 7.83 and 11.74 dB on CelebA and CARS; absolute PSNR values not provided, so multiplicative factor cannot be calculated
